description: Selects the Data Archive table to work on, for example pipoint, piarc or pi_gen,pitimeout. Commands start with @ (the default command character), comments with *, and the default field delimiter is a comma.
Sets the operation mode for the following data lines: list, create, edit or delete. Scripts also use a ', t' suffix (for example @mode create, t).
verifyNote: The meaning of the ', t' suffix (believed to make piconfig tolerant of existing points) and the full mode list are not confirmed in a readable reference.

description: Defines the input structure: the order of fields in the data lines that follow.
Defines the output structure: which fields are listed.
Selects the records to act on, for example tag=*. Several selections can follow one structure, each closed by @ends.
notes: Command abbreviations such as @tabl, @sele and @modi are seen in examples; the abbreviation rule itself is inferred.

description: Ends a command block and executes the selection.
Ends the piconfig session.
Reads data lines from a file, or writes listing output to a file.
In an edit script, sets field values for the records read from the input, for example to mark archive values bad.
notes: piconfig cannot filter an archive query for a particular value; find the bad values first with DataLink, PI OLEDB Provider, SMT Archive Editor or an AF SDK utility.

description: Sets the point class used when creating points, for example classic.
Changes the field delimiter from the default comma.
Controls echoing: Data, Commands, All, Verbose or None (default Data).
Sets the input type (F, D or K; default D).
verifyNote: The meanings of F, D and K were not read.

description: In non-interactive mode piconfig stops after the number of errors set by @line, so check the output for errors after bulk imports.
verifyNote: The default value and exact semantics are unclear in the source.

description: Help: ?atr lists the attributes of the current table and ?tbl lists the tables.
Other piconfig commands listed in the reference: case handling, change directory, clear settings and end of record.
verifyNote: Only the command names were read; check each command's behaviour in the piconfig reference.

description: Lists tag names with their PointIDs into a file. Archive files store PointIDs, not tag names; the map is in the PIPOINT table.
Lists archived values of a tag for a time range from the piarc table.
Creates classic points from data lines that follow the input structure.
verifyNote: The ', t' suffix is not confirmed in a readable reference.

description: Deletes the tags listed after the input structure. Point deletion takes a global lock; run bulk deletes off-hours. There is no undelete.
verifyNote: The deletion script was seen as a snippet only.

description: Changes a point's class by editing ptclassname on the PIPOINT table.
verifyNote: The thread gives the structure but not the exact script.

command: Enable the Data Archive audit trail (script)
description: Sets the EnableAudit tuning parameter in the pi_gen,pitimeout table. -1 audits all databases; per a 2010 blog the value is a bit mask by subsystem database.
verifyNote: Whether the bit values are current for recent Data Archive versions is not confirmed.

description: Snapshot statistics, refreshed every 5 seconds (Ctrl+C to exit).

Event queue statistics, every 5 seconds. Total Event Reads and Writes should rise together; more than one event queue file suggests a problem. A growing queue means the archive subsystem is not keeping up.
Archive statistics, every 5 seconds. The Archiving flag is 0 none, 1 historic only, 2 future only, 3 both; 3 is healthy on Data Archive 2015 and later (1 on 2012 and earlier).
Lists archives and shows archive-shift progress. Run from the adm folder.
Thread dump of the archive subsystem; use the Connection IDs to find heavy clients in Network Manager Statistics.
Backs up the latest n archives (-numarch <n>) or a list of archive numbers (-archives <list>). It cannot take a range of older archives.
verifyNote: Only the -numarch and -archives options are sourced; the full syntax (including the backup path argument) was not read.

description: Queries backup status (from a community answer).
Checks licensing and tests the PI License Manager (pilicmgr). Run from %PISERVER%\adm. With pilicmgr down it returned [-10727] PINET RPC is non-existant.
Waits until a subsystem is ready; pisrvstart.bat runs piartool -block pisnapss -verbose. A hang there pointed to a corrupt snapshot table.
Registers an archive file. Registration is per host: run it on the Data Archive whose registration you want to change (each collective member separately).
Brackets a file copy of a subsystem file (such as the audit file piarchssaudit.dat) so it can be copied safely.
example:
piartool -systembackup start -subsystem piarchss
copy d:\pi\log\piarchssaudit.dat d:\pi\adm\archaudit_Copy.dat
piartool -systembackup end -subsystem piarchss

description: Checks an archive file and shows its storage map, including the PointIDs it contains.
Checks localhost.tz (DST rules). After DST rule changes, patch the OS and update localhost.tz.
Dumps the full DST history.
Translates an error code into its message.
notes: The adm research could not confirm this from a readable AVEVA page, but a PI Square blog shows it.

description: Dumps an archive header; the primary archive shows End Time 'Current Time'.
Registers the primary archive (used during a restore).
Reports Data Archive TLS certificate registration.
Registers (changes) the Data Archive TLS certificate.
Reads a copy of a Data Archive audit file for a time range.
Follows the PI Message Log continuously. Run from PIHOME\adm on clients or %piserver%\adm on the Data Archive.
Reads messages for a time window.
Filters by minimum severity (information, warning, error, critical); the default minimum is Debug.
notes: The mapping of each switch letter to a severity name is inferred from the letters.

description: Output as CSV (-fc), two-line (-ft), one-line (-fw) or XML (-fx); -oa shows all fields. Default fields are MessageSeverity, MessageTime, ProcessHost, ProcessName, Source1-3, Message and MessageID.
-msg filters by message text with * and ? wildcards; -src and -pr filter by source or program; -top pr or -top pid gives summary counts; -of writes to a file.
notes: The example combines sourced switches to find ArcMaxCollect hits; the combination itself is inferred.

description: PIBackup.bat calls AFBackup.bat for AF. The AF SQL backup runs the stored procedure dbo.usp_backup on the PIFD database. PI Backup uses VSS, so files in use can be backed up without downtime.
notes: Back up daily off-peak with Windows Task Scheduler, locally first, then copy to a separate server.
verifyNote: The pibackup.bat arguments and default folder were not read.

description: Shows the overall PI Buffer Subsystem status (connected, events being sent).
Shows buffer queue statistics (Ctrl+C to stop). A healthy queue has reads and writes; with a collective it asks which member's queue to show.
Stops or restarts sending buffered data, for example to simulate a network outage.
Command-line status and shutdown utility for the legacy API Buffer Server (bufserv).
PI API tool for checking snapshots and connectivity from an interface node.
Tests Performance Equation syntax.
Site-specific stop script: edit pisrvsitestop.bat rather than pisrvstop.bat. AVEVA bulletins advise monitoring the services started by \PI\adm\pisrvstart.bat.
Checks that the Data Archive port is reachable from a client. Data sent to the Data Archive uses TCP 5450.
notes: The Test-NetConnection form is named in the playbook; its exact arguments are standard PowerShell.

description: AVEVA GitHub sample for a silent PI Server install.
Changes the AF Server TLS certificate (/CertificateThumbprint:). It is stored as CERTIFICATETHUMBPRINT under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\AFService.
Turns on the AF audit trail (/AT). SQL Server Agent must be running first, and you need sysadmin on the SQL instance hosting the AF database.
Exports and imports AF databases as XML. The utilities are in \PIPC\AF on the client.
Creates the HTTP SPNs for PI Vision's service account; create one for the short name and one for the FQDN.
example:
setspn -U -S http/pivis01 CORP\svc-pivision
setspn -U -S http/pivis01.corp.example CORP\svc-pivision

description: Lists SPNs on an account, or queries an SPN. The Data Archive SPN class is PIServer; the AF class is AFServer.
Clears cached Kerberos tickets. For troubleshooting, first set LogLevel (REG_DWORD 1) under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\Kerberos\Parameters and then review the System event log.
Checks which services an account may delegate to (constrained delegation).
Lists the cmdlets of PowerShell Tools for the PI System (module OSIsoft.PowerShell, shipped with PI SMT 2015 and later, auto-imported on first use).
Opens a connection to a Data Archive; other cmdlets take it with -Connection.
Reads point configuration by name or ID.
Reads values at a time, over a range or by count. Timestamps display in UTC.
notes: As of August 2015 PI relative times such as * could not be used.

description: Writes values; it appends unless -WriteMode is given. As of 2015 writes could not be buffered.
notes: The full -WriteMode value list was not read.

description: Changes point attributes.
Lists archive files (Index, StartTime, EndTime, PercentFull, IsCorrupt, Path and more) and registers or unregisters them.
Starts a Data Archive backup and polls its progress ($state.IsInProgress, $state.BackupProgress.OverallPercentComplete). "Backup-PIDataArchive" does not appear in any source seen.
notes: Start-PIBackup also supports -Exclude, e.g. -Exclude pimsgss, SettingsAndTimeoutParameters (seen in a snippet).

description: Reads the PI Message Log from PowerShell.
EdgeCmd is the Edge Data Store CLI that translates commands into REST calls (EDS listens on port 5590 by default). This verifies an install.
